description:
Latent sibling of fz-9in, found while auditing jobs/backend.rs lower_step. The runtime-demand walk (jobs/runtime_demand.rs) demands BinaryOp/UnaryOp operands WHOLE only when the result value's demand is not Ignore -- but backend emission packages BinaryOp/UnaryOp steps UNCONDITIONALLY (no construction_step_or_omitted gate, deliberately: arithmetic can trap, e.g. division, so eliding it would change observable abort semantics). That pair of facts is the same starvation shape fz-9in had: if a trap-capable op ever survives into a body whose result is undemanded, the emitted step reads operands that were never materialized -> 'backend value N is unbound' on interp / bound-before-use panic in native lowering.

NOT currently reproduced: unused pure ops appear to be folded or dropped before backend emission (probe: fn main() with unused y = 1 + 2 beside dbg(Enum.take(xs,3)) passes on interp at 2b5451677; the fz-9in repro only reached the crash because the construction lived in a SEPARATE allocating callee whose call edge survived). Acceptance: either (a) prove unreachable -- show every path that emits a BinaryOp/UnaryOp step guarantees its operands carry demand (e.g. because a trap-capable op is always treated as observable/demanded, or pure ops with Ignore results never reach emission), and pin that invariant with a test/debug assertion; or (b) close the hole by construction -- make emission and demand agree: an op step retained for its trap semantics must force WHOLE demand on its operands (demand follows retention, not result-liveness). Do NOT blanket-omit: an unused 1/0 must still abort. Try to build a cross-executable repro first (mirror fz-9in: an allocating or otherwise call-surviving callee whose body ends in an undemanded trap-capable op reading its params).
title: BinaryOp/UnaryOp steps emitted unconditionally with Ignore-demanded operands -- latent operand-starvation (fz-9in sibling)
